Notes

A warning about the social world becomes a consumer report on its damaged people. The speaker moves between contempt, worried affection and the decision to withdraw.

天太热了

The song opens with bodily discomfort before offering social advice. Later it tells the listener not to cry when the heat makes them sweat, blurring two kinds of moisture on a face. That small confusion prepares a track where expressions are unreliable and it is difficult to tell what people genuinely feel.

  • Lyric transcript
听了不记

听 and 记 distinguish receiving words from retaining them. The advice demands both, then insults the listener who fails. This is guidance with pressure built into it: experience is transmitted as a warning, and any later suffering can be blamed on the person who did not remember the rules.

  • Lyric transcript
不学无术

艺术, yìshù, ends with the same shù that closes 不学无术, bùxué-wúshù: having neither learning nor skill. The reply seizes the last sound of “art” and returns it as an accusation of incompetence. English carries the contempt but loses this quick verbal catch, where the lofty claim supplies the material for its own dismissal.

  • Lyric text
清白

清白 means innocent or untainted, literally clear and white. It follows 清醒, being clearheaded, and precedes the accusation of pretending to be innocent. The shared 清, qīng, sound briefly builds an image of clarity before the next lines expose it as an act. The sequence lets pristine language do the work of camouflage.

  • Lyric transcript
连连看

连连看 is a tile-matching game: identify repeated pictures and pair them away. It arrives immediately after “they all look the same,” making the surrounding people seem as interchangeable as game pieces. The narrator’s small private pastime becomes a way to judge a scene full of supposedly distinctive personalities.

  • Developer description: 連連看 on Google Play
  • Lyric text
消费者观察报告

The phrase sounds like the heading of a sober report. Surrounded by judgments of faces, manners and rotten hearts, it turns watching a social scene into inspecting merchandise. The later gold-and-rotten-stuffing proverb returns to exactly that problem: what the polished exterior advertises versus what the thing contains.

  • Lyric transcript
没处撒野的器官

撒野 is behaving wildly or acting out without restraint. Giving that impulse to organs strips away the people’s respectable faces and leaves frustrated bodily drives. The line follows malice stored up for half a lifetime, so the behavior appears as pressure seeking an outlet rather than as an impressive form of freedom.

  • Lyric transcript
江湖

江湖, jiānghú, literally means rivers and lakes, but also names the wider social world a person has to navigate. It carries the sense of informal rules, experience and entanglement captured in the saying about not being free to act as one pleases within it. Here that world becomes a poison: belonging has entered people’s bodies and altered them.

  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 江湖
  • Lyric transcript
水帘洞

水帘洞, Water Curtain Cave, is the hidden home reached through a waterfall in the first chapter of Journey to the West. Entering it establishes the stone monkey’s authority among the other monkeys. The name brings that childhood-familiar fantastic space into a verse of smoke and half-sleep; it offers a refuge-like image just after the claim that the social world has poisoned people.

  • Journey to the West, chapter 1 (Shidetang edition)
  • Lyric text
时代变了

This familiar announcement often promises modernization or progress. The next two lines make its conclusion simply that things are worse. The deadpan turn refuses to let novelty count as improvement, just as the song refuses to let a polished look count as inner worth. The speaker’s test is what the change does to people.

  • Lyric transcript
金玉其外败絮其中

This phrase comes from Liu Ji’s parable of an orange seller: beautiful fruit contains pulp as dry as worn cotton wadding, and the seller compares it to impressive-looking officials who fail the people. Its everyday meaning is an attractive exterior hiding poor substance. Here it caps a catalog of innocent faces and respectable appearances, giving the judgment a long satirical ancestry.

  • Ministry of Education idiom dictionary: 金玉其外，敗絮其中
  • Lyric transcript
小祖宗

小祖宗, “little ancestor,” addresses someone with a mixture of fondness, deference and exasperation, as if the troublesome younger person must be served like an honored elder. After dismissing an entire crowd as ruined, the speaker suddenly sounds worried about a particular person. The maze and the failed rescue that follow make the affection hurt rather than simply soften the insult.

  • Genius community transcript
迷宫

Unlike an open road, a maze offers movement without a clear way out. One careless entrance traps the person; seeing their stumbling from outside does not give the narrator a route to rescue them. This is the song’s most sympathetic image of jianghu: a social world can ruin someone without that person fully understanding its layout.

  • Lyric transcript
爱莫能助

The segmentation is 可 / 爱莫能助: “but / willing to help yet unable to.” 可爱 is not “cute” here. The idiom preserves the speaker’s concern even as it admits powerlessness, which makes the following physical and emotional withdrawal more conflicted than a simple refusal to care.

  • Lyric text
物理隔离

隔离 repeats after three modifiers: physical, biological, emotional. The technical-sounding sequence makes withdrawal resemble a procedure carried out in stages. Yet it follows “I see all of your pain” and “I cannot help,” so the final emotional separation is the hardest step. Distance is being constructed because care alone has not made rescue possible.

  • Genius community transcript
骚

骚, sāo, can describe sexual boldness, but colloquial praise also uses it for conspicuous flair or an outrageous move. “Flashy” captures that showy excess. After the long withdrawal into emotional isolation, the short exclamations suddenly sound like a spectator reacting to somebody’s display, with admiration and mockery still entangled.

  • Lyric text

About Jackzebra and this mixtape

Zhuang Zhuang Mixtape arrived on Surf Gang on October 2, 2026: 55 tracks, opening with Sour and closing with Sweet. Its cast widens from YoungQueenz on Poker Face to User116, Effie, kuru, yoyi, 春 and 南部犯罪份子. Aghast has a production credit on every track from Hitman through Snatch, giving that stretch a shared collaborator behind its changing scenes.

Surf Gang release · Artist credits

Jackzebra told AVYSS that he writes while singing over a beat he has listened to repeatedly, keeping the images in his head central. He values the room Mandarin leaves for indirect meanings. Listen for ordinary phrases becoming physical scenes: familiarity becomes cooking, authority becomes family seniority, and a tired saying suddenly turns into a threat.

AVYSS interview, 2024

In STATIC, he describes mixtapes as a format for letting ideas flow, reserving an official debut album for later. In a separate conversation about Above & Beyond, he compared that earlier tape to a collection of his producer friends’ work. The credits here likewise reward attention: long-running collaborators sit alongside guests working in Mandarin, Korean and English.

STATIC interview · Sabukaru interview, 2025

The small details connect to his stated interests: he has described playing Temple Run in transit and before shows, watching Top Boy, and wanting to score White Oleander. These give the songs specific points of contact with his life. The notes follow those connections alongside the lyrics’ jokes, invented scenes and competing voices.

His recommendations in Perfectly Imperfect · Dazed interview, 2025 · Interview questionnaire, 2025

Jackzebra has pushed back on being made to represent all of China’s underground. These notes stay close to the words: what an expression usually means, what changes in this line, and how another song answers it. Cultural references have sources; interpretations rest on details you can hear or read in the song.
